Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 26-year-old woman with 3-day, moderate-to-severe (8/10) headache, maximal around right eye, dull with intermittent sharp exacerbations.  
• Associated photophobia, transient visual “shooting lights,” nausea without vomiting, functional impairment.  
• No fever, neck stiffness, focal neurologic deficits, or trauma.  
• Family history of migraine (mother, sister).  
• Ibuprofen at sub-maximal dose ineffective.  

Working diagnosis  
• Migraine, possibly with aura — strongly supported by symptom pattern, family history, and DDx (high likelihood).

Considerations  
• Tension-type headache (medium likelihood per DDx) given diffuse dull component and work-related stress.  
• Acute sinusitis (low–medium) less likely; lacking nasal or febrile features.  

Plan  
• Educated on appropriate NSAID dosing: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg two tablets three times daily or prescribe Naproxen (dose not documented—pending prescription).  
• Add simple analgesia (Paracetamol) and consider short course of Codeine-containing combination if pain persists.  
• Headache diary to identify triggers.  
• Safety-net: return urgently for vision changes, focal weakness, worsening pain, or systemic symptoms.  
• Follow-up in 1–2 weeks; consider prophylactic migraine therapy if recurrent.  
• Encourage routine eye examination to assess for visual strain.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed correct NSAID use; advised monitoring hydration and screen brightness; smoking cessation and alcohol moderation not specifically counselled—education pending  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of current headache; avoidance of future migraine episodes  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not applicable/Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Optometry referral advised for eye test; Quitline referral to be considered at future visit if smoking continues  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Review in 1–2 weeks; sooner if red-flag symptoms occur  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not required at this stage; monitor stress levels  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Neurology referral if headaches become frequent or refractory  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Recommended  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine with aura – High likelihood. Classic unilateral pain, photophobia, visual scintillations, nausea, strong family history.  
2. Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood. Diffuse dull pain and work stress but lacks classic migraine features.  
3. Acute sinusitis – Low–Medium likelihood. Periorbital pain but lacks sinonasal symptoms or fever.
